MCU card: STM32C5A3VGT6 (144 MHz, Ethernet, 2× CAN-FD, crypto, no
TrustZone) ≈ 300 + 16 MB QSPI NOR (log + OTA) + RTC with CR2032

magnetics ≈ 200 (owner figure), ESD + passives ≈ 70
4 analog inputs, 0–10 V / 4–20 mA (no PT1000): op-amps, 0.1 % resistors,
mode FETs, protection, 0.1 % 2.5 V reference
6 digital inputs: single optocouplers (LTV-217 / EL3H7 class), IEC
61131-2 Type 3; 2 pulse counters
6 relays SPDT 10 A, 230 VAC / 30 VDC, 5 kV reinforced, INR 40 each (owner
target); ULN2803, watchdog gating, snubbers

each incl. holder (owner)

sense, TVS, reverse FET
18 relay terminal poles, 5.08 mm, 300 V / 10 A, kept apart from the low-
voltage terminals

109, protection, switchable termination, terminal
USB-C service port (5 V, no PD) + LEDs

common

Passives

Notes
• LoRa selling price INR 1,600 (owner, 2026-11-19), read as price after profit without battery board and adapter: needs
a BOM of ≤ INR 687 at 100 pcs, now 1,154 — a 40 % cut.
• Fieldbus controller, two models (owner, 2026-11-25), incl. power stage and enclosure: with Ethernet 2,650, without
Ethernet 2,530 (spreadsheet ranges 2,650–2,700 / 2,530–2,590) — over the INR 2,000 limit by 530–650.
• MCU cards: STM32C5A3 standard; STM32H573 (PSA L3) or Renesas RA6M4 (classic CAN) as options. Motor control on a
separate card (D-41). LoRa redesigned as a remote IO node (owner, 2026-11-19): STM32WLE5 at INR 250, 2-layer PCB, 16
MB QSPI NOR for its own OTA and logging (2026-11-23), RS-485 + 4 DI + 4 AI + 4 DO (low-power high-side quad), SMA
antenna kept for long range — BOM 1,154. Tip: volume quotes (≈ −10 %) → ≈ 1,039; no relays: their coils would drain
the battery.
• Tip — every module: this is a high-volume product, so negotiate the big parts with distributors (modem, ESP32-C6
module, MCUs, isolated transceivers, enclosures); the BOMs here are still research prices × 1.3 at 100 units.
• Adapter (owner, 2026-11-18): one 12 V 18 W adapter per stack or standalone module; a full 4-module stack peaks at ≈
13–14 W with charging capped at 0.3 A per battery board.
• Not included: development amortisation — at 100 pieces every INR 1 lakh of NRE per module type adds INR 1,000 to its
cost and ≈ INR 1,300 to its price after profit; distributor margin (left to the client / partner).
